The published panel\textquotesingle s \texttt{gpt-5-nano} seat and its \texttt{DeepSeek-V4-Flash} checkpoint, which NHR@FAU replaced on 2026-08-01, are not used here.
\emph{Score} is the reported metric, the per-essay median over the panel; \emph{Debiased} is the same median after each related judge\textquotesingle s tier effect is subtracted and mapped back onto its own scale, and $\Delta$ is the gap between them.
$\Delta$ is blank where no judge was related to the model at all, which is a different statement from the $0.0$ of a model that was corrected but whose median did not move.
Both ensemble score columns are shaded on the same scale as the judge columns, so the correction is visible as a step in colour;
$\Delta$ is left unshaded rather than given a second scale of its own.
\emph{Bias} gives the closest relation the model has to any judge on the panel, most severe first where there is more than one: $\mathrm{M}$ same model, $\mathrm{F}$ same family (same vendor and version series), $\mathrm{V}$ same vendor; blank means related to none of them. The one $\mathrm{F}$ row is the retired 0423 DeepSeek checkpoint judged by 0731: same vendor, same version series, different weights.
The bold cell with a matching superscript in the judge columns is the judgement that relation concerns, so the column says \emph{whether} and the superscript says \emph{where}.
